editorial.headline: Beyond the Vacancy: Indonesia’s Other Employment-Placement Activity
editorial.standfirst: This code covers vacancy recording, referrals and job placements outside an employer relationship—and remains open to PMA nationally and in Bali, with address-specific verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 78109 is an employment-placement activity centred on the movement from vacancy to placement. Its scope includes recording vacancies, referring people to work opportunities and placing workers into a job. The defining boundary is straightforward: the people placed are not employees of the placement company itself. That makes the code about matching and placing labour, rather than employing the labour being placed. The scope expressly includes casting-agency work—selecting performers for theatre and similar productions—and talent-search activities. In practical terms, it describes a placement function spanning job opportunities, performance selection and talent discovery.

Registration is available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The record therefore places no scale-based exclusion on the activity across those four categories. For founders, that is a useful starting point: the stated scope remains the same whether the operation is modest or large. Yet the operational identity should remain precise. A business using this code is registering a function of vacancy recording, referral or placement; it should not blur that function with an employer relationship when workers are placed. Casting and talent search sit within the same stated perimeter, provided the work remains the selection or placement activity described here.

Across Indonesia, the PMA position is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%. Put plainly, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. No lower national ownership ceiling is stated in this record, so the national picture is clear: foreign investment is open for the activity at the stated 100% ceiling. This ownership position attaches to the activity itself; Bali’s province-level position is considered separately.

In Bali, the record’s result is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and it is not blocked by the moratorium. The reason given is that this is a medium-high/high-risk activity, placing it outside the permanent, island-wide Bali moratorium that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA. The Bali outcome is therefore not a reversal of the national position: PMA registration is open in Bali today for this activity. The record nonetheless directs verification for the particular address. That is an address-specific check, not a Bali-wide prohibition or an alternative foreign-ownership ceiling. The conclusion is firm but disciplined: this code is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the stated moratorium.
